findings.issue_text: In packages/core/EventManager.ts:119, destructuring the first element of the destinationCalendar array and accessing `.integration` without optional chaining throws a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty, crashing booking creation for Google Meet location bookings with no destination calendar set

In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~line 256), the fallback lookup `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only reached when externalCalendarId is already falsy, making the predicate never match and causing selectedCalendar to resolve to undefined, breaking calendar event updates when no explicit externalCalendarId is passed

In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts deleteEvent (~line 317), the same dead-predicate bug as the updateEvent issue causes calendarId to resolve to undefined, breaking Google Calendar event deletion when no explicit external calendar id is supplied

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts (~line 1077), `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar was initialized to null, silently dropping all collected team members' destination calendars for COLLECTIVE events

In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts createEvent (~122) and updateEvent (~228), the organizer attendee's email/externalId is always taken from the first destination calendar array entry regardless of which host's credential is being processed, causing non-first hosts in a collective booking to get the wrong organizer email/externalId

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts (credential DB fallback, ~430-445), the prisma.credential.findUnique fallback query omits `app: { select: { slug: true } }` and doesn't construct appName, unlike the equivalent fallback added in EventManager.ts, causing getCalendar() to be unable to resolve the correct calendar service

In packages/core/EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents (~338+), calendar creation for multiple destination calendars now runs sequentially in a for-await loop instead of being parallelized, making booking latency scale linearly with the number of hosts/destination calendars on collective events

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts loadUsers (~722-760), validation failures are thrown as plain Error objects instead of HttpError, causing the catch block to misclassify client-input errors as a generic 500 instead of a 400

In packages/core/EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents catch block (~593-596), the console.error(message) call from the original code was dropped when rewritten to map over multiple calendarReferences, silently losing error logging on this failure path

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/core/EventManager.ts:119, destructuring the first element of the destinationCalendar array and accessing `.integration` without optional chaining throws a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty, crashing booking creation for Google Meet location bookings with no destination calendar set

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and adds `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` but then immediately does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array (which the diff explicitly allows/creates in multiple places, e.g. `destinationCalendar: []`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~line 256), the fallback lookup `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only reached when externalCalendarId is already falsy, making the predicate never match and causing selectedCalendar to resolve to undefined, breaking calendar event updates when no explicit externalCalendarId is passed

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is computed as:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

The `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (because of the ternary), so the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` is effectively comparing against `undefined`/`null`. That will almost always return no match, yielding `selectedCalendar` as `undefined`. This is a concrete logic error introduced by the diff and can cause calendar updates (and similarly the delete logic below) to target no calendar ID / fall back incorrectly when no explicit `externalCalendarId` is provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts deleteEvent (~line 317), the same dead-predicate bug as the updateEvent issue causes calendarId to resolve to undefined, breaking Google Calendar event deletion when no explicit external calendar id is supplied

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the new fallback branch is:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied (undefined/null), the `find` predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, so it will almost always return `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains valid calendars. That changes behavior from the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback and can cause deletion to target the wrong calendar (likely falling back to "primary" later) or pass an undefined calendarId, breaking deletion for events created on non-primary calendars when no explicit external calendar id is provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts (~line 1077), `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar was initialized to null, silently dropping all collected team members' destination calendars for COLLECTIVE events

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` and a specific line where `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` allegedly becomes a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. That file and code are not present anywhere in the provided diff, so the claim cannot be verified against the changes shown. The diff only shows updates to other files (e.g., `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `EventManager.ts`, calendar services) and does not introduce or demonstrate the cited `push(...)` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts createEvent (~122) and updateEvent (~228), the organizer attendee's email/externalId is always taken from the first destination calendar array entry regardless of which host's credential is being processed, causing non-first hosts in a collective booking to get the wrong organizer email/externalId

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent the calendarId used for insertion is selected by matching destinationCalendar[].credentialId === credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is set from `mainHostDestinationCalendar` which is always the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`. That means when EventManager creates multiple events (looping through destinationCalendar entries for collective bookings), non-first destination calendars will still use the first destination calendar’s externalId as the organizer email. The same pattern exists in updateEvent: organizer email comes from the first destination calendar entry regardless of which externalCalendarId/credential is being updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts (credential DB fallback, ~430-445), the prisma.credential.findUnique fallback query omits `app: { select: { slug: true } }` and doesn't construct appName, unlike the equivalent fallback added in EventManager.ts, causing getCalendar() to be unable to resolve the correct calendar service

adjudication.rationale:
The diff shows `handleCancelBooking.ts` now falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then passes the returned record directly into `getCalendar()`. Unlike `EventManager.ts`, it does not `include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}` nor construct a `{ appName: ... }` wrapper.

However, from the diff alone it is not verifiable that `getCalendar()` requires `appName` (or an included `app.slug`) to resolve the calendar service. The code already previously passed `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.find(...)` results into `getCalendar()` without constructing `appName`, implying `getCalendar()` likely keys off `credential.type`/`key` rather than an `appName` field. Therefore the claim that this omission will make `getCalendar()` “unable to resolve the correct calendar service” is speculative based on code not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/core/EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents (~338+), calendar creation for multiple destination calendars now runs sequentially in a for-await loop instead of being parallelized, making booking latency scale linearly with the number of hosts/destination calendars on collective events

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `createAllCalendarEvents` to iterate `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and performs `await createEvent(...)` inside that loop (when `destination.credentialId` is present). This makes those calendar creations run sequentially rather than concurrently. Since `destinationCalendar` is now an array (collective/multi-destination scenarios), overall booking latency will increase roughly linearly with the number of destinations/hosts, unlike the prior parallel `Promise.all(...)` pattern used elsewhere in the function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts loadUsers (~722-760), validation failures are thrown as plain Error objects instead of HttpError, causing the catch block to misclassify client-input errors as a generic 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding refers to `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` (specifically `loadUsers` around ~722-760) and behavior of throwing `Error` vs `HttpError`. None of that file or code path appears in the provided diff. The diff only shows changes in `handleCancelBooking.ts` and various calendar services/types. Therefore this issue cannot be verified as being introduced or present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/core/EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents catch block (~593-596), the console.error(message) call from the original code was dropped when rewritten to map over multiple calendarReferences, silently losing error logging on this failure path

adjudication.rationale: The diff in packages/core/EventManager.ts shows the error path was rewritten to handle multiple calendar references. In the catch block, the original `console.error(message);` line is removed (it appears in the removed lines and is not present in the new code). The new catch block only returns mapped failure results without logging, so failures on this path will no longer be logged, matching the finding.
